subject.title: feat: heading-aware chunking + entity extraction for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw implement heading-aware memory chunking now as a narrow memory-core change, and should it be default behavior or an opt-in strategy/config surface?
rationale: Current source proves the retrieval-quality gap, but the durable answer changes memory index identity and may add config/default behavior; the entity extraction stretch also crosses privacy, graph-memory, and plugin-slot product boundaries.

options.title: Narrow Chunking First
options.body: Implement only heading/section-aware chunking after choosing default versus opt-in semantics, update index identity/reindex behavior, and leave entity graph work for a separate tracker.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Memory MVP
options.body: Keep the issue open but defer implementation until the memory schema, write pipeline, and operator facade decisions in the MVP issues converge.

options.title: Route Entity Graph Out Of Core
options.body: Treat graph/entity extraction as plugin, QMD, Honcho, or ClawHub work unless a missing OpenClaw memory API is identified.

recommendation.title: Narrow Chunking First
recommendation.body: Implement only heading/section-aware chunking after choosing default versus opt-in semantics, update index identity/reindex behavior, and leave entity graph work for a separate tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage, SDK, and index identity history makes this handle the best available routing candidate for the memory lifecycle/product boundary choice.
